author: Brendan Fanning at the Aviva Stadium
description:
• Ireland 20-17 South Africa

  • Sam Prendergast’s penalty proves the winning margin

Not long ago a man I know was barred from a local charity shop. For haggling. He wasn’t trying to put a hole in their profits, he explained, rather it was in his blood to drive for a harder bargain whatever the circumstances. He couldn’t help it.

That was the attitude of the Springboks here a year ago when they had Ireland on toast and kept demanding more rounds. It’s in their blood too.

Continue reading...
title: Ireland stand firm to beat South Africa but Erasmus’s men head to final

author: Kaz Therese, as told to James Norman
description:
Kaz Therese had always loved An Affair to Remember. A few months into their relationship, Brianna surprised her with a magical gift

  • Find more stories from the moment I knew series

Brianna and I met in 2013 on an arts project I was developing in Mount Druitt, the region I grew up in, in western Sydney.

It was a site-specific work for young people, and Brianna became part of the strategic leadership team, which ultimately meant she was painting gutters pink with the local kids until 9pm each night.

Continue reading...
title: The moment I knew: She flew me to the scene of my favourite romantic movie

author: Guardian Staff
description:
• Dortmund beat Mönchengladbach in Bundesliga

  • Harry Kane vows to return after Bayern injury

Lazio continued to underline their Serie A title credentials with a comfortable 3-0 ⁠home win against Lecce as Gennaro Gattuso’s side remained unbeaten this season and extended their lead ⁠at the top ⁠of the ​standings.

Tijjani Noslin scored in each half and Davide Frattesi wrapped up the win in style with a 90th-minute ⁠strike as Lazio earned their 10th victory in 12 games to move to 32 points, four ahead of Inter ⁠who travel to Atlanta on Sunday. Como are fourth on 26 points after ​a 2-0 win against Cagliari ‌thanks to goals from ‌Jacobo Ramón and Lucas Da Cunha.

Continue reading...
title: European football: Noslin’s double helps Lazio extend Serie A lead; Nmecha sends Dortmund top

author: Donna Ferguson
description:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of FBI’s most wanted fugitives and evaded capture for more than a decade

The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s top 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that sparked widespread panic in the city of Guasave.

Continue reading...
title: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid

author: Gerard Meagher at Allianz Stadium
description:
Storied full-back’s celebration turns to ash and New Zealand risk more than Rennie’s wrath unless they bounce back

If their punishment last week was to be told in no uncertain terms that they had let the country down, what awaits the All Blacks after this? Public humiliation? Exile? A firing squad at dawn? That New Zealand followed head coach Dave Rennie’s rebuke with their worst Twickenham performance of the professional era and a record defeat by England suggests such criticism monumentally backfired.

Perhaps it is wise to remember it is only a game, Dave. For what made the very best All Blacks sides so impressive was that they always looked like they were having fun. That they would showcase the most mesmerising skills and do so with a smile on their faces took the breath away and added to the allure. This rabble did not look like they were having much fun out there.
title: Fading Beauden Barrett a symbol of rabble All Blacks’ joyless decline | Gerard Meagher

author: Tumaini Carayol
description:
• Winner claims 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) victory in semi-final

  • Second seed rallies past American after sensational 7-1 tie-break

The man himself was not present in Turin on Saturday afternoon, but one of the most intriguing developments on and off court in men’s tennis this year was Ben Shelton’s surprise decision to hire the former No 1 Juan-Carlos Ferrero as his new coach alongside his father, Bryan. Ferrero is one of the most highly respected coaches on tour, but he also knows Carlos Alcaraz better than any other coach in the world.

However, there is only so much that anyone can do against one of this sport’s greatest talents. Shelton, the third seed, played a spectacular match, serving monstrously, attacking without hesitation and particularly volleying so well in decisive moments, but it still wasn’t enough to defeat the second seeded Alcaraz, who maintained his focus after an uncertain start as he reached the final of the ATP Finals with a
title: Carlos Alcaraz holds off Ben Shelton to book place in ATP Finals

author: Press Association
description:
• Scotland 67-5 Japan

  • Ollie Smith also scores two tries for the hosts

Darcy Graham and Liam McConnell inspired a much-changed Scotland to a comfortable 11-try Nations Championship victory against a meek Japan.

Graham moved on to the 41-try mark for his country with a hat-trick as he moved six clear of Duhan van der Merwe at the top of the national team’s all-time scoring charts. McConnell also enjoyed a day to remember as the 22-year-old back-rower broke his Scotland duck with a treble of his own.

Continue reading...
title: Graham and McConnell hat-tricks fire 11-try Scotland to crushing win against Japan

author: Robert Kitson at Allianz Stadium
description:
• England 37-12 New Zealand

  • Slade scores the first of five tries for England

Every year the All Blacks come to south-west London it feels like an acid test. And rarely, if ever, have England responded with such class and conviction on this famous old stretch of grass. New Zealand simply could not live with their clear-eyed, motivated opponents who, at times, made their illustrious visitors look horribly second-rate.

If Kiwi fans thought last week’s loss to Wales was painful this was arguably as bad in terms of the reputational damage. The home side were 19-0 up after 36 minutes and had the game all but wrapped up within a couple of minutes of the restart when Ollie Chessum smashed his way over to claim his side’s fourth try. From a margin of victory perspective this was England’s biggest victory over New Zealand in the 121-year-o
title: Slade helps sparkling England power to record victory as All Blacks wilt again

author: Reuters
description:
Death adds to national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years

Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 ⁠on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for the infectious disease, the state’s health department said.

The department said the child was ⁠age four or younger. It did not disclose additional details, including the child’s vaccination status, citing the family’s privacy.

Continue reading...
title: Virginia child dies in state’s first measles-associated death of 2026

author: Patrick Daly
description:
Joshua Foster tells of moment he ‘lost control’ of two-year-old when he fell from fourth storey of hotel

A British father who was fined by the courts after his two-year-old son fell from a fourth-floor window during a family holiday in Cyprus has recalled his “despair” when the boy slipped from his grasp.

Joshua Foster was handed a €3,000 (£2,500) penalty after he pleaded guilty to a charge of causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act. Prosecutors in Cyprus had refused to drop the case against him.

Continue reading...
title: British man recalls ‘despair’ over son’s death after fall from Cyprus window

author: Suzanne Wrack
description:
Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea, the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point. After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night, Chelsea drew a blank.

Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after beating City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short.

This story will be updated after London City Lionesses v Crystal Palace

Continue reading...
title: Liverpool keeper Keating holds leaders Chelsea at bay in scoreless WSL draw

author: Sara Braun
description:
The viral satirization of the caregiving burden left to women and daughters hit home for many viewers

The Saturday Night Live sketch, titled Sister quickly went viral this week for its satirization of the burden that women and daughters face to take care of aging family members. In the parody commercial, comedian John Mulaney touts the benefit of “Sister”, who he describes as “a live-in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister” .

“Now I don’t have to worry about dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life, and the stuff I like to do,” Mulaney says, as the sister, played by cast member Jane Wickline, gives their father’s medication to him.

The sketch, which amassed over seven million views on YouTube in less than a week since it aired, has
title: SNL’s skit Sister captures the quiet agony of caregiving for women: ‘I’ve never felt seen like that’

author: Sam Levin in New York
description:
Rev Dr Jeff Hood stood at the side of Reinaldo Dennes as the state of Texas put him to death, calling the experience ‘overwhelming’

“Take me, father!”

It was one of many cries Reinaldo Dennes uttered on Thursday night as he lay strapped to a gurney inside a Texas death chamber while prison officials struggled, for more than an hour, to carry out his execution.

Continue reading...
title: Witness recounts a botched execution in Texas: ‘Just such horror and terror and pain’

author: Press Association
description:
• Southampton 2-0 Derby; Norwich 2-1 Cardiff

  • QPR get first away win since August at 10-man Millwall

Cyle Larin returned to action with a bang as Southampton extended their unbeaten run at home in the Championship to 18 games with a 2-0 victory over second-bottom Derby.

Larin turned in his eighth goal of the season but his first since 12 September – after a four-game drought and a hamstring problem. Divin Mubama added a second in stoppage time as Saints shrugged off worries of failing against lower-placed sides – having dropped points against Watford, Preston, Wrexham, Lincoln and Bolton already this season.

Continue reading...
title: Championship roundup: Southampton get Larin lift as Norwich win five in a row

author: Harry Cockburn
description:
Documentary records Catherine taking on Three Peaks challenge and finding ‘sense of hope alongside uncertainty’

The Princess of Wales has spoken candidly about the impact of her cancer diagnosis in a BBC documentary to be aired later this month.

“Cancer does change you,” Catherine, 44, says in the trailer for the 30-minute programme. “It changes your body. It changes you physically, but there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

Continue reading...
title: Princess of Wales speaks about impact of cancer diagnosis in BBC film Heal

author: Will Unwin at the Etihad Stadium
description:
Manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four but at least ended their three-game losing run against Fulham. As they await the fate of their much-publicised appeal after being found guilty of financial breaches, their form has slumped as further evidenced by a passive draw.

Arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more. The Norwegian uncharacteristically missed a number of fine chances as Rodrigo Muniz took advantage of City’s porous defence, who had to rely on Elliot Anderson to get anything out of the fixture.

Continue reading...
title: Elliot Anderson ends Manchester City’s losing run but boos greet Fulham draw

description:
Latest intrusions targeted farmer-payment system at the USDA and the FBI’s National Crime Information Center

Hackers breached the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the FBI, national media reported on Friday, amid deepening concerns over a spate of tech outages at key American institutions.

The breaches were first reported by NBC News and CNN respectively, and it remained unclear whether they were related and who was responsible.

description:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’

Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control on the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am on Saturday morning, after all night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the Review Conference on Conventional Weapons at the UN in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

author: Ali Martin at the Melbourne Cricket Ground
description:
At the end of a bruising week for Australian cricket came a few hours of respite and a night that ended with roars of delight inside the MCG. Set 188 to win, a home side light on star names beat England by three wickets and with one ball to spare.

The off-field developments had kept coming before the start of play. Cricket Australia had publicly thrown its support behind Pat Cummins as Test captain, while broadcast partners Fox Cricket decided it was probably in everyone’s interest to stand down Usman Khawaja and David Warner from commentary duties.

Continue reading...
title: Chaudhary guides Australia to gripping T20 opener win over Brook-inspired England

author: Dr Robert Mote
description:
I was bullied for my deafness as a child, and just when I was finding myself, a car crash set me back years. But then I watched the movie Better Man, and had my life explained for me

I cannot say I’ve ever been a Robbie Williams fan. When I went to see Better Man, the 2024 biopic in which Williams is played by a CGI chimp, I was tagging along with my wife. To be honest, I was sceptical about the ape but tried to meet the film with an open mind. I wasn’t looking for anything in particular but what I found was something that seemed to explain my life.

I was born two months premature in Winnipeg, Canada, in 1961, with severe hearing loss in both ears that wasn’t diagnosed until I was seven. In 1969 we moved to Woking in Surrey; my father left and my mother descended into alcoholism. I was a misfit in my family, with no support for my deafness, and at school the bullying – from kids and teachers – was something awf
title: A Robbie Williams film starring a CGI chimp helped me come to terms with my hearing loss

author: Rev Kevin Deal
description:
Humans experience beauty and sit with mysteries. Unlike AI, we do not exist merely for utility

Last month, religious leaders from across San Francisco gathered behind closed doors to discuss what it means to be human in the age of artificial intelligence.

Anthropic, the AI company operating only a couple of miles from my parish, has been courting priests, rabbis and theologians. Its billionaire cofounder, Christopher Olah, has even pressed Vatican advisers to take seriously the possibility that his company’s chatbot might possess consciousness.

Continue reading...
title: I’m a priest. Silicon Valley’s search for the ‘soul’ of AI is deeply troubling | Rev Kevin Deal

author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
description:
Canadians have put a lot of trust in their prime minister but some question if it can last if the trade wars were to end

In the hours after polls in the US midterm elections closed and it became clear that Donald Trump had been rebuked in historic fashion, Canadian politicians were elated.

“I was doing cartwheels down the street, and have you ever seen a big guy like me doing cartwheels?” said Ontario premier Doug Ford, a prominent critic of American tariffs.

Continue reading...
title: Mark Carney is so popular he can get away with a lot. Will it last if the Trump spell breaks?

author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
description:
Manchester-based Megatone Sound Foundation and Baron Turbo Charge have rejuvenated the culture to offer a sense of belonging and empowerment

For a generation of young Black Mancunians, some of the history lessons that mattered most were not taught in classrooms, but through towering stacks of amps and speakers, turntables and Jamaican records.

“We didn’t know where we fit in. We didn’t know our history. Our parents were busy working two or three jobs,” says Errol “Barzy” Beaumont, a founder member of Baron Turbo Charge, Manchester’s long-running reggae sound system. “It was the records – Burning Spear, Bob Marley, Culture, that were telling us about our culture, which wasn’t on the school curriculum. For us, the sound system was not just entertainment – it was an education.”
title: ‘Music was our teacher’: the sound system pioneers reviving the scene in Manchester and beyond

author: Ben Knight
description:
When the humpback got stranded on Germany’s Baltic coast, crowds gathered, conspiracy theorists pitted themselves against scientists and animal lovers argued with vets. Why did the animal trigger such an intense derangement?

What surprised Bodo Köpnick was how loud the whale was. “You could hear it as far away as the next village. It was eerie, but also impressive,” he says, then pauses to think how best to describe the noise a suffering humpback makes at night. “It was like a cow moaning. It went to your marrow.”

Köpnick, 65, is everything you would hope for in a volunteer fire chief on a sleepy holiday island: a grandfatherly figure who mostly spends his weekends teaching local children about health and safety, and letting them climb on the engines. But on 31 March his life was made infinitely more stressful by the appearance of a lost whale that had got itself stranded on the shores of his island of Poel, in northern Germany. It became his fate to stand on the shorel
title: ‘People couldn’t deal with watching an animal die’: the strange saga of Timmy the whale – and how a whole country lost its mind

author: Ben Quinn and Rowena Mason
description:
Thursday’s byelection in Castle Bromwich will be latest test for Nigel Farage’s party as rival eats into support

Voters go to the polls in the village of Castle Bromwich this Thursday in a little-noticed election that is the latest test for Reform at a time when it is particularly vulnerable.

Yet, while it is the Conservatives who are edging ahead in recent national polls, the decisive difference could well be the performance of Restore Britain – the hard-right party set up by Rupert Lowe after the MP fell out with Farage.

Continue reading...
title: Reform UK considers pact with Restore Britain to overcome stalling performance in polls

author: Etienne Côté-Paluck in Port-au-Prince and Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
description:
Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation

A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.

In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was
title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs

author: Robert Booth in New York
description:
Director and Scorsese collaborator is using AI in films and sees its takeover as inevitable, not just in cinema

Paul Schrader was sipping white wine in a Greenwich Village trattoria when he said how he felt about using AI to make films: “I am opening the cage of a monster and I don’t have a leash.”

The 80-year-old film-maker behind Taxi Driver, Raging Bull and American Gigolo, is embracing the technology as he enters the final act of a prolific career in which he has collaborated with Martin Scorsese, Robert De Niro, Sigourney Weaver and Richard Gere.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’m opening the cage of a monster’: Taxi Driver scriptwriter Paul Schrader on unleashing AI at 80

author: Fanni Szakál
description:
A heatwave in the Bering Sea that killed 10bn snow crabs has led to a new species emerging that has no fishing quotas

Somewhere out on the Bering Sea, hundreds of miles off the coast of Alaska, a group of researchers onboard the trawler Alaska Knight haul up a heap of crabs from the seabed. As they sort and measure their haul, something seems wrong.

The catch, which usually features species such as the snow crab – a species of spider crab growing up to a metre wide with its legs outstretched – or its larger relative, the tanner crab, is instead dominated by an odd-looking hybrid of the two species.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Legally, they don’t exist’: the hybrid crabs puzzling biologists and fishers

author: Grace Holliday
description:
The photographer hopes his intimate photograph of two sleeping birds will remind others of their special person

Twenty-one-year-old Noah Forster had always thought swans were beautiful, but it was his girlfriend Cecilia is the one who made him really notice them. The pair began dating two years ago, but now live 70 miles apart; he is a welder in Newark-on-Trent, she is studying law in Leeds.

“The distance can be difficult, but we try to talk as much as possible,” Forster says. “It’s taken me a while to save up for a driver’s licence and car, so I have a daily walk from my home and across the River Trent to get the 6am train to work. We like to send photos of our day to each other, and I took this photo on an exceptionally cold and frosty morning in November, walking across the river to get to work. I saw these swans near the castle. Napping together on the reeds, they appeared luminous.”
title: ‘Napping together on the reeds, the swans appeared luminous’: Noah Forster’s best phone picture

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Grassroots group Women Against Rape says ‘things are really changing’ in how victims are treated by criminal justice system

When Mr Justice Bennathan sentenced Russell Brand to 10 and a half years in prison, there was a notable shift in the characterisation of victims of sexual assault. “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no, and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent,” the judge said.

In 1977 it was a completely different story. Justices Roskill, Wien and Slynn allowed the convicted rapist Queen’s Guardsman Tom Holdsworth to walk free on appeal after his rape conviction because of his “promising army career”. The same year, Judge Zigmond gave the rapist of a three-year-old girl just a suspended sentence, telling her
title: ‘No means no, however we dress and wherever we go’: 50 years of campaigning against rape

title: Sam Lau on Robert Pattinson’s cinematic ubiquity – cartoon

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
The party invested in key battlegrounds, netting stunning wins at the expense of candidates in Florida and Louisiana

To call it a blue wave, said the Florida governor, Ron DeSantis, would be an epic understatement. The midterm elections were “the political equivalent of a meteor strike”. But one state, DeSantis added with pride, was able to “hold the line”. And that state was Florida.

On a night when almost everything else went right for Democrats, David Jolly fell short by 1.3 percentage points against Republican Byron Donalds, who will become Florida’s first Black governor, while Angie Nixon, bidding to become the state’s first Black senator,
title: Did Democrats fail Florida? Angie Nixon on ‘missed opportunity’ in midterms

author: Rosanna Greenstreet
description:
The TV presenter on his costly divorce, his ‘stupid’ hair, and why his driving licence is on life support

Born in Solihull, West Midlands, Richard Hammond, 56, attended Harrogate College of Art and Technology and began his broadcasting career in local radio. He went on to become a presenter for the Men & Motors TV channel and, from 2002 to 2015, he was part of the BBC’s Top Gear team with Jeremy Clarkson and James May. In 2016, the trio started to host The Grand Tour for Amazon Prime. Since 2021, Hammond has presented the restoration programme, Richard Hammond’s Workshop, which is in its sixth season and available on Quest. He is divorced with two daughters and lives in Monmouthshire, Wales.

When were you happiest?
Whenever I’m either walking on a mountain fell, or on a motorcycle.

Continue reading...
title: Richard Hammond: ‘I’m much taller than you think. I’m just standing further away’

author: Andrew Lawrence
description:
Netflix documentary Primetime Preacher$ travels back to a time when evangelism found a dominant place on US television – and the shocking tabloid stories that followed

For three decades, film-maker Joe Berlinger has gripped true-crime buffs with his deep dives into small-town murders and infamous serial killers. His Netflix explorations of John Wayne Gacy and Jeffrey Dahmer helped flip documentary storytelling from viewer homework to a welcome distraction.

After dedicating so much time to the life of Jeffrey Epstein, the kidnapping of JonBenét Ramsey and other unsolved mysteries, Berlinger thought Primetime Preacher$, his new Netflix documentary on America’s televangelist boom, would offer a break. But it turns out that’s a pretty juicy crime story too, about the religious right’s bank job on American politics. “The deeper resonance for me came when I realized that the global televangelism rise actually mirrors the rise of the religious right,” he says. “Religion and po
title: ‘Shakespearean tale of ego, greed and ambition’: the scandalous story of televangelism

author: Martin Pengelly
description:
New memoir tells of policy feats and battles with Trump but struggles to take responsibility for re-election debacle

Inevitably, readers of Joe Biden’s new memoir will flick forward to find what he says about the events that ended his presidency: increasing pressure about his age and capacity that finally led him to stand aside and anoint Kamala Harris, too late, ushering fascism back to the White House. Alas, Biden thinks he was just fine to keep on serving and the whole thing was a stitch-up by a panicked party.

Of his catastrophic debate in June 2024, when the then 81-year-old president blinked, stuttered and gaped under the lights, Biden writes: “I knew the debate had gone badly. But I knew that debates had gone badly for lots of incumbent presidents. Especially their first ones. I left the stage thinking I would be debating Trump once more before the election was over. I was
title: Promise Me, America by Joe Biden review – former president defends his decisions

author: Ola Szwarc, Nadim Amin, Konstantin Filippou, and Felix Mandl – as told to Joanna Taylor
description:
Some of the city’s best chefs, Ola Szwarc, Nadim Amin, Konstantin Filippou and Felix Mandl, share their favourite cafes, bars and restaurants

There are two sides to coffee in Vienna. The grand, old-school coffee houses are incredible places to sit, have breakfast, drink a beer and forget about time. They have much the same function as a pub in Britain. For that experience, we’d go to Café Prückel or Café Hawelka. For a quintessential Viennese coffee, we’d suggest a wiener melange – somewhat similar to a cappuccino, but traditionally a little milder, made with coffee, steamed milk and milk foam. Alternatively, an einspänner is another p
title: Vienna on a plate: a food lover’s guide to the Austrian capital

author: Robyn Vinter and Josh Halliday
description:
Campaigners call out ‘greed’ of developers after 95% of ‘megashed’ planning applications approved in last 10 years

When a planning application for a lot next to his new home landed in his letterbox, Jon Davis was crestfallen.

He had just moved into the property in Bingham, Nottinghamshire, with his wife and toddler in June.

Continue reading...
title: ‘National scandal’: residents in England rally against surge in mega-warehouse developments

author: Sarah Marsh and Nicola Davis
description:
Experts say BBLs and other cosmetic procedures can be risky and seasonal offers at clinics in England could make people rush decisions

Clinics in England are promoting seasonal deals – including for Black Friday – on liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), despite concerns about the risks of the procedure.

The government is consulting on limiting liquid BBLs, vampire facials and deep chemical peels in England to qualified healthcare professionals.

Continue reading...
title: Black Friday deals for liquid Brazilian butt lifts criticised over safety fears

author: Harry Taylor
description:
All options open in future talks, says Ed Miliband, while prime minister hails ‘a good day for Britain and Europe’

The UK rejoining the EU could be on the table in informal discussions between Andy Burnham and European leaders in Brussels, Ed Miliband has said.

The foreign secretary said “all options” would be examined in the process, after the prime minister agreed deals on trade and young people with the bloc on Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Rejoining EU ‘on the table’ as UK strikes deals on trade and young people

author: Giles Richards in Las Vegas
description:
• Antonelli quickest in qualifying but will start from sixth on grid

  • Verstappen starts on front row alongside Mercedes’ George Russell

Kimi Antonelli was quickest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, but the newly-crowned world champion will not be on pole for Sunday’s race as he has a five-place grid penalty for taking a new engine for this meeting. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who was second, will take pole – his first in Las Vegas – and Mercedes’ George Russell will line up alongside him on the front row of the grid after finishing in third. Antonelli will start from sixth.

Lando Norris was fourth for McLaren and Isack Hadjar fifth for Red Bull. The Ferrari was not in good shape in Las Vegas however. Lewis Hamilton was struggling with a lack of grip throughout the session and could not hook up a good lap. Neither he nor his teammate Charles Leclerc could make it out of Q2, with Leclerc finishing in 11th and Hamilton in 12th. They w
title: Max Verstappen takes pole for Las Vegas Grand Prix after Kimi Antonelli penalty

author: Kayode Akintola
description:
The outbreak in DR Congo is shaping up to be the worst ever, but the support of local faith leaders – and adequate funding – will be needed to bring it under control

Ebola is terrifying: I know, because I lived through the world’s worst outbreak of the disease. That was in west Africa between 2013 and 2016, when anyone infected by the virus had a nearly 40% chance of dying.

There were 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths then. Now a rare strain of Ebola is spreading in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, much more quickly than a decade ago in Sierra Leone, Liberia and neighbouring countries. It is the 17th outbreak in DR Congo and already its worst, with more than 5,000 deaths. The UN is warning that the spread of the disease is outstripping th
title: Beating Ebola takes more than medicine – I saw what worked in west Africa a decade ago | Kayode Akintola

author: Tim Dowling
description:
Finding a rat relaxing in my late father-in-law’s cottage is unnerving. As always, my wife takes command of the situation

In the year since my father-in-law died my wife and I have visited his cottage, on average, every other week – more often in spring and summer. In theory, this is often enough to keep abreast of appointments with people coming to deal with various issues: slipped roof slates, fallen trees, electrical problems. In practice, more can go wrong than gets put right in the interval.

This time we’ve been away for three weeks. My son was meant to go down, but his plans changed. We need to be there to meet someone measuring up for two replacement windows, and whatever else.

Continue reading...
title: Tim Dowling: there’s been a break-in, and I have to remove the culprit

author: Jenny Kleeman
description:
The one thing stopping AI taking over the world – or at least everyone’s jobs? Dexterity. Human hands are anatomical marvels that engineers have struggled for years to replicate. Experts are racing to change that

Just outside Luton, in an Amazon warehouse the size of four football pitches, yellow shelving units pirouette in a digitally choreographed dance. Tubs containing a Lego Spider-Man kit, followed by dishwasher tablets, followed by a pouch of muscle building protein powder whiz along conveyor belts, until they arrive at a human being tasked with stacking the shelving unit that has come to a stop in front of their workstation. This, Amazon says, is the “symphony of people and technology” to which the retail giant owes its success.

Following a barrage of negative publicity about working practices, Amazon began to open up
title: ‘The doom of humanity’: will the quest to make robotic hands render us obsolete?

author: Esther Addley
description:
After the Brand and Walliams revelations, calls for a ‘staggered’ age of consent are redefining what makes someone ‘adult’

The fact that the age of sexual consent in Britain is set at 16 is thanks to a chimney sweep’s daughter from Marylebone, London, called Eliza Armstrong – not that she had any say in the matter.

In June 1885, Armstrong had just turned 13 when she was sold for sex by her alcoholic mother for the sum of £5. She believed she was going to work as a gentleman’s maid; instead, the child was taken to a brothel, where she was examined to prove she was a virgin and drugged with chloroform to await the gentleman who had “purchased” her virginity.

Continue reading...
title: Consent under scrutiny: where does youth end and adulthood begin?

author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv; photographs by Julia Kochetova
description:
Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yet

Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.

Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.

Continue reading...
title: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges

author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
description:
Charity that collects the coins says donations are down by £200,000 after a barrier was put in place to restrict access

When Jeff Clinton, an American visiting Rome with his wife for the first time, found a US one-cent coin on a street close to Termini train station, he knew precisely what he was going to do with it. “I’ll throw it into the Trevi fountain,” said Clinton, holding the copper coin in the palm of his hand as the couple admired the landmark.

He was well aware of the tradition among tourists of tossing a coin over their shoulder and into the waters of the baroque masterpiece, in a ritual fabled to ensure a return visit to the city or make other dreams come true.

Continue reading...
title: Tourists are throwing fewer coins into Rome’s Trevi fountain – is €2 entry fee to blame?

author: Jason Burke, and Seham Tantesh in Gaza
description:
Floods have worsened harsh existence for Palestinians living in tent camps, with fears growing for what the coming months will bring

Abdul Karim al-Sahhar knew winter was coming to Gaza in the small hours of a wet and windy night earlier this month when a sandbank collapsed just yards from his makeshift tent, killing four people.

“It was a terrifying scene. I could not process what I was seeing,” the 30-year-old said. “My legs felt frozen from the shock. I found my mother buried under the sand.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We ​are tired from all this suffering’: displaced families in Gaza brace for another winter of misery

author: Gordon Brown
description:
As Spain heads into a critical election, polling shows that many voters attracted by rightwing parties don’t really agree with their ideas

When Spain goes to the polls on 29 November, its citizens will be the first of some 200 million people in Europe eligible to vote in the following 12 months; 2027 will be a year of elections – including France, Poland, Estonia and Italy – which will be critical to the future of Europe. This will be the biggest electoral test in nearly 100 years of the s
title: The far right is menacing Europe – but it is fragile. What the extremists and voters want isn’t the same | Gordon Brown

author: Kaamil Ahmed
description:
Survivors recount rivers red with blood and burning nearby villages serving as an urgent warning to flee their homes

Smoke was often the signal to run – seen from a distance, it was the indication for Rohingya that a neighbouring village was under attack and that theirs would be next.

In other places, they saw the rivers run red and would pull out the bodies, perform quick burial rites and then flee.

Continue reading...
title: Rohingya who escaped Myanmar’s genocide tell their stories

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time

Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.

The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A new record for entertainment’: Grand Theft Auto VI sales hit $3.8bn on first day of release, developer says
